about: The launcher's files that Cartouche's console on the Mac does not link (builder/mac/Sources/CartoucheConsole/Shared), each with why: 'iphone', the iPhone's alone; 'mac', the Mac has its own, named; 'later', it comes to the Mac at that step of the plan (docs/decisions.md, 95). A new file of the launcher is linked in Shared, or listed here: app/tests/test_mac_console.py checks it.

CartoucheAccount.swift.why: The Apple ID the built-in SideStore signs Cartouche and its games with on the iPhone; a Mac game is signed by nxnative's build, and the console's stand-in says so.

CartoucheArrangement.swift.why: The console and a game's sheet side by side on an iPhone Duo unfolded: the Mac's window puts them side by side itself.

CartoucheContinuedWork.swift.why: iOS's background transfers (BGContinuedProcessingTask): the Mac's app goes on in the background on its own.

CartoucheDevice.swift.why: This iPhone's model, GPU, the memory limit iOS sets and the signature's end: the Mac's own in the console's stand-ins.

CartoucheDeviceWords.swift.why: An iPad's words for the device Cartouche runs on, which CartoucheText.s applies under #if canImport(UIKit): the Mac's own come from strings.json.

CartoucheGameActions.swift.why: LiveContainer's steps (install, start, uninstall a game): the Mac starts the game's app through the app (MacGames), as the console's stand-in asks it.

CartoucheGameHost.swift.why: A game running behind the console in LiveContainer's LiveProcess: a Mac game runs in its own window.

CartoucheGameInfoView.swift.why: What the player says of a game (its name, genre, summary, cover): with the game's settings on the Mac.

CartoucheGameOrientation.swift.why: Which ways a game behind the console turns the screen: a Mac's screen does not turn.

CartoucheGameSettings.swift.why: A game's own settings in the console: on the Mac, nxnative's own window shows them meanwhile (Game settings).

CartoucheGamesView.swift.why: The Games tab that holds the console on the iPhone: the Mac's window holds the same screens.

CartoucheGuide.swift.why: The way to a first game on a new iPhone (LocalDevVPN, Apple ID, a Mac): the Mac's is the Builder's setup assistant; the console's stand-in shows no guide.

CartoucheGuideView.swift.why: The first game's guide over the iPhone's console (CartoucheGuide).

CartoucheImportPicker.swift.why: The Files picker an IPA is imported with: on the Mac, Import opens the Builder, which adds games.

CartoucheImportedSigning.swift.why: The certificate an iPhone's games are signed with, imported: a Mac game is signed by nxnative's build.

CartoucheInstallQuestions.swift.why: The question an install asks on an iPhone whose GPU cannot read BC textures (A16 and older): every Mac Cartouche runs on reads them.

CartouchePickerMeasures.swift.why: What Cartouche can measure of iOS's Files picker.

CartoucheProblemReport.swift.why: System › Report a problem: with the console's reports and measurements on the Mac.

CartoucheRelease.swift.why: Cartouche's versions as the built-in SideStore's source lists them: the Mac's app updates itself from its own releases.

CartoucheRenewal.swift.why: Renewing the free account's 7-day signature on the iPhone: a Mac app does not expire.

CartoucheReportView.swift.why: System › Report a problem, its screen: with the console's reports and measurements on the Mac.

CartoucheReporting.swift.why: The report under each error and its Copy the report button: with the console's measurements on the Mac; the console's stand-in keeps the Builder's own reports meanwhile.

CartoucheRootView.swift.why: Cartouche's screens in place of LiveContainer's tab bar: on the Mac, the app's window and its switch between the console and the Builder.

CartoucheRunningGame.swift.why: A game behind the console and its memory: on the Mac, the game's own app, followed by MacGames, as the console's stand-in says.

CartoucheSaveBackups.swift.why: The games' saves kept in step with the saves folder: on the Mac, with the same CartoucheSaveSync, by MacSaves.

CartoucheSetup.swift.why: The iPhone's setup: pairing file, Apple ID and certificate for SideStore and LiveContainer.

CartoucheSetupFacts.swift.why: What the iPhone's setup says to the measurements (app.opened).

CartoucheSignInView.swift.why: The Apple ID sign-in for the built-in SideStore.

CartoucheSigningMaterial.swift.why: The certificate and profile an iPhone's games are signed with.

CartoucheSigningView.swift.why: Choosing how the iPhone's games are signed.

CartoucheStorageDriveView.swift.why: The player's Google Drive on the Storage page: with the console's storage and the library the iPhone and the Mac share.

CartoucheStorageMacView.swift.why: Pairing the iPhone with a Mac, from the iPhone's side: the Builder's iPhone page is the Mac's side.

CartoucheStorageSFTP.swift.why: An SFTP server of the player's: with the console's storage and the library the iPhone and the Mac share.

CartoucheStorageSMB.swift.why: A shared folder over SMB: with the console's storage and the library the iPhone and the Mac share.

CartoucheStorageView.swift.why: The Storage page: with the console's storage and the library the iPhone and the Mac share.

CartoucheSystemView.swift.why: The System page: with the console's settings on the Mac; System opens the Builder meanwhile.

CartoucheTV.swift.why: The game alone on a TV while the iPhone keeps its controls: a Mac shows the game on any of its displays itself.

CartoucheTelemetry.swift.why: Cartouche's measurements of the games: the console's own on the Mac, told apart from the iPhone's on the dashboard; the Builder measures the Mac's builds and games meanwhile (builder.*).

CartoucheTelemetryView.swift.why: System › Game measurements: with the console's measurements on the Mac.

CartoucheUpdateView.swift.why: Cartouche's own update over the console, through SideStore: the Mac's app updates itself.

CartoucheUpdates.swift.why: Cartouche's own updates, through SideStore: the Mac's app updates itself.

CartoucheVPN.swift.why: Whether LocalDevVPN is on, which SideStore needs on the iPhone.
